boundary_rationale: The fifth and final header of this chapter opens the row in the asher-hayah OAN shape rather than the lamed-initial pattern of its neighbors: “Yahweh's word that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning Elam” (web:Jer.49.34), spliced אֲשֶׁ֨ר הָיָ֧ה דְבַר יְהוָ֛ה אֶל יִרְמְיָ֥הוּ הַנָּבִ֖יא אֶל עֵילָ֑ם (oshb:Jer.49.34, byte tier), dated within the same verse to “the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah”, rendering בְּרֵאשִׁ֗ית מַלְכ֛וּת צִדְקִיָּ֥ה מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָ֖ה (oshb:Jer.49.34, byte tier) -- bereshit malkhut Tsidqiyah, a construct distinct from the bereshit-mamlekhet date frames used elsewhere in this book's narrative chapters, and written here in this name's short form (4 verses book-wide against 44 for the long form Tsidqiyahu). A koh-amar-tsevaot onset follows immediately at 49:35, “Behold, I will break the bow of Elam”, spliced כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת הִנְנִ֥י שֹׁבֵ֖ר אֶת קֶ֣שֶׁת עֵילָ֑ם (oshb:Jer.49.35, byte tier), continuing through the four-winds scattering (Jer.49.36, which also carries a ketiv/qere note on "Elam" itself, consulted per the inventory but not spliced here), the dismay-and-sword declaration (Jer.49.37, which carries two paseq marks per the inventory, single-witness and unlocated within the verse), to the throne-in-Elam image closing 49:38 -- one continuous first-person divine speech about Elam with no addressee directly spoken to and no fresh formula reintroduced after 49:35. This span's front seam is Jer.49.33 (SAMEKH), a single-witness mark; within this Prophets book such marks are graded tier-3, the corroboration scale's weakest step -- closing the Kedar-and-Hazor oracle just before it opens.

A setumah closes Jer.49.39, single-witness like every parashah mark in this book; the Prophets grading holds it at tier-3, the weakest corroboration step, so it corroborates rather than drives the back seam between this coda and the Babylon oracle opening at Jer.50.1; no mark-layer entry falls at this row's own front seam, Jer.49.38|Jer.49.39.

device_notes: The two ketiv/qere notes at Jer.49.39 sit on different form classes: the first pair corrects a verb (the ketiv אשוב corrected by the qere אָשִׁ֛יב, both oshb:Jer.49.39, byte tier), and the second pair corrects the object noun the verb governs, standing after the object marker את (the ketiv שבית corrected by the qere שְׁב֥וּת, both oshb:Jer.49.39, byte tier); the pointed qere text is the tier consulted for the gloss above, with each ketiv's consonantal form spliced and named beside it. Read consecutively, the qere sequence אָשִׁ֛יב … אֶת … שְׁב֥וּת (oshb:Jer.49.39; not itself a contiguous run in this verse's own bytes, since the unpointed form שבית stands between the object marker and the pointed noun) matches, token for token under the read forms only, the contiguous run אָשִׁ֛יב אֶת שְׁב֥וּת (oshb:Jer.49.6, byte tier) closing the Ammon coda; the two written forms at Jer.49.39 differ from that run at both tokens, so the identity is qere-borne only.

boundary_rationale: “The word that Yahweh spoke concerning Babylon, concerning the land of the Chaldeans, by Jeremiah the prophet” (web:Jer.50.1) opens the row, spliced הַדָּבָ֗ר אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֶל בָּבֶ֖ל אֶל אֶ֣רֶץ כַּשְׂדִּ֑ים בְּיַ֖ד יִרְמְיָ֥הוּ הַנָּבִֽיא (oshb:Jer.50.1, byte tier) -- hadavar asher dibber, a header shape distinct from both the vayehi and hadavar-asher-hayah word-event forms used elsewhere in this book and from the asher-hayah OAN header opening the previous unit at Jer.49.34, marking the Babylon oracle's own onset. A discourse-frame imperative follows in the same scene: “Declare among the nations and publish” (web:Jer.50.2), rendering הַגִּ֨ידוּ בַגּוֹיִ֤ם וְהַשְׁמִ֨יעוּ֙ (oshb:Jer.50.2, byte tier), reporting Babylon's fall as an accomplished fact through the name of one of its gods: “Babylon has been taken, Bel is disappointed” (web:Jer.50.2), spliced נִלְכְּדָ֨ה בָבֶ֜ל הֹבִ֥ישׁ בֵּל֙ (oshb:Jer.50.2, byte tier). A setumah closes Jer.49.39, the Elam restoration coda opened by the header at Jer.49.34, immediately before this chapter opens -- single-witness, and, as with every parashah mark in these Prophets chapters, no stronger than tier-3. No mark-layer entry falls inside Jer.50.1-Jer.50.3, and the segment opening after MT 49:39 runs past this unit's own back seam at Jer.50.3|Jer.50.4 -- disclosed, single-witness and tier-3 per this book's Prophets-wide weak-corroboration rule, and never counterevidence in either direction.
